ops.title: Synced-credential install: owned-precedence resolution
ops.body:
The "why" behind pool.InstallSyncedCredential (internal/pool/credinstall.go) and hostsync.installEnvelope (internal/hostsync/materialize.go), trimmed out of their godocs (terse-comment rule).

Both install a stripped (refresh-token-free) credential pulled from a peer, under identical owned-precedence rules:

- **Owned local wins outright.** An owned local blob (refresh token present) on ANY backend is never overwritten or shadowed, even when expired — forking off a peer's synced copy would strand the owned chain. InstallSyncedCredential blocks only on `HasRefreshToken()`; installEnvelope treats any present cred at all as changed-underfoot (no row exists yet, so any credential in the slot means a concurrent `ccp add` login is landing).
- **Empty/tombstone always installs.** ErrNotFound / ErrNoTokens ⇒ the slot is a proven install target.
- **Unprovable fails closed.** A read error other than not-found/tombstone/unavailable aborts with ErrCredentialUnverifiable — writing over an unreadable slot could destroy a credential we cannot see.
- **Unsearchable keychain ⇒ file fallback.** creds.ErrUnavailable (headless login keychain, absence unprovable) retargets the write at the plaintext file store rather than aborting; owned-before-synced still resolves an owned chain that later surfaces there.
- **Synced-vs-synced ⇒ strictly-fresher-expiry wins** (InstallSyncedCredential only).
- **CAS write.** The write goes through writeCredCAS under the account lock (re-proves the slot empty / prev-token-matched at write time), so an underfoot `claude /login` aborts as a clean skip (ErrCredentialChangedUnderfoot). Residual re-read→write TOCTOU vs an in-session claude is tracked in ccn task 4ed1146.

The shared Store.Read error taxonomy is now a first-class classifier: creds.ClassifyRead(err) → ReadState (ReadPresent / ReadEmpty / ReadUnsearchable / ReadFatal), routed at all four error-arm sites (InstallSyncedCredential loop, writeCredCAS, installEnvelope's kc+file reads, slotRetainsCredential) so the sentinel handling can't drift. The "present" tail legitimately differs per site and stays hand-rolled.
